objects.description: Signed 64-bit file offset type used for stream seeking/telling within this API.
Signed 64-bit timestamp type; in this API it represents 100-nanosecond intervals since 1601-01-01 for entry modification times.
Opaque handle for a read-only input stream. Represents data sources backed by FILE, filesystem paths, memory buffers, or platform streams. Lifetime is managed by ar_close.
Forward declaration of a Windows COM IStream interface used to open an ar_stream via ar_open_istream. Definition is external to this header.

Opaque handle for an opened archive abstraction (RAR/TAR/ZIP/7z). Provides iteration over entries, metadata access, and decompression of entry data. Created from an ar_stream by format-specific open functions and freed with ar_close_archive (does not close the underlying ar_stream).

functions.name: ar_open
functions.description: Opens a read-only unarr stream that wraps an existing FILE*. Use it as the input source for archive open functions. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: f must be a valid, open FILE* positioned at the intended start of data.
The returned ar_stream is read-only.
Close the stream with ar_close when finished.
Do not use the FILE* directly for I/O after giving it to ar_open, to avoid desynchronization (inferred from typical stream wrapper patterns).

functions.name: ar_open_file
functions.description: Opens a read-only unarr stream for the file at the given path. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: path must be a valid, non-NULL C string path to an existing readable file.
Close the stream with ar_close when finished.

functions.name: ar_open_memory
functions.description: Opens a read-only unarr stream over an in-memory buffer. The data pointer must remain valid until ar_close is called. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: data must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least datalen bytes.
datalen must accurately reflect the buffer size.
The memory referenced by data must remain valid and unchanged until ar_close is called on the returned stream.
Close the stream with ar_close when finished.

functions.name: ar_close
functions.description: Closes the stream and releases underlying resources. After this call, the stream must not be used.
requirements: stream must be a stream returned by an ar_open*/ar_open_* function or NULL (behavior for NULL is unspecified; avoid passing NULL).
Do not use stream after calling ar_close.

functions.name: ar_read
functions.description: Reads up to count bytes from the stream into buffer, advancing the read offset. Returns the actual number of bytes read.
requirements: stream must be a valid, open ar_stream.
buffer must point to a writable region of at least count bytes.
count may be zero.
Handle short reads; fewer than count bytes may be returned at EOF or on partial availability.

functions.name: ar_seek
functions.signature: bool ar_seek(ar_stream *stream, off64_t offset, int origin);
functions.description: Moves the read offset pointer similarly to fseek. Returns false on failure.
requirements: stream must be a valid, open ar_stream.
origin must be a valid seek origin (SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, or SEEK_END).
offset is interpreted relative to origin and may be negative when origin is SEEK_CUR or SEEK_END (off64_t is signed).
Do not seek within an archive between ar_parse_entry and the final corresponding ar_entry_uncompress call (see API warning).

functions.name: ar_skip
functions.description: Convenience for ar_seek(stream, count, SEEK_CUR). Advances or rewinds by count bytes. Returns false on failure.
requirements: stream must be a valid, open ar_stream.
count may be positive (forward) or negative (backward).
Do not seek/skip within an archive between ar_parse_entry and the final corresponding ar_entry_uncompress call (see API warning).

functions.name: ar_tell
functions.description: Returns the current read offset in the stream, or 0 on error. Note that a legitimate position of 0 is indistinguishable from an error using this function alone.
requirements: stream must be a valid, open ar_stream.
Callers should disambiguate a 0 return (start-of-stream vs. error) via additional context or prior successful operations.

functions.name: ar_close_archive
functions.description: Frees all data associated with the given archive handle. Does not close the underlying ar_stream.
requirements: ar must be a valid ar_archive returned by an ar_open_*_archive function.
Do not use ar after calling ar_close_archive.
Call ar_close separately on the underlying ar_stream if you own it.

functions.name: ar_parse_entry
functions.description: Reads the next archive entry. Returns false on error or when reaching the end; use ar_at_eof to distinguish EOF from error.
requirements: ar must be a valid, initialized archive.
Do not manually seek in the underlying stream between ar_parse_entry and the last corresponding ar_entry_uncompress call (API warning).
On false return, use ar_at_eof(ar) to determine if EOF was reached.

functions.name: ar_parse_entry_at
functions.description: Reads the archive entry at the given offset (as returned by ar_entry_get_offset). Offset 0 restarts at the first entry. The call should always succeed.
requirements: ar must be a valid, initialized archive.
offset must be either 0 or a value previously obtained from ar_entry_get_offset for this archive.
Do not manually seek in the underlying stream between parsing an entry and completing its uncompression (API warning).

functions.name: ar_parse_entry_for
functions.description: Locates and reads the (first) archive entry with the given name. Returns false if not found.
requirements: ar must be a valid, initialized archive.
entry_name must be a valid, non-NULL UTF-8 string representing the desired entry name.
Name matching semantics beyond first match are unspecified.

functions.name: ar_at_eof
functions.description: Indicates whether the last ar_parse_entry call reached the archive's expected end-of-file.
requirements: ar must be a valid, initialized archive.
Call after ar_parse_entry returns false to distinguish EOF from error.

functions.name: ar_entry_get_name
functions.description: Returns the UTF-8 name of the current entry. The returned pointer is valid only until the next call to ar_parse_entry. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: ar must refer to a current, successfully parsed entry.
Do not retain or use the returned pointer after the next ar_parse_entry call; copy it if needed longer.
Treat a NULL return as a failure to retrieve the name.

functions.name: ar_entry_get_offset
functions.description: Returns the stream offset of the current entry for use with ar_parse_entry_at.
requirements: ar must refer to a current, successfully parsed entry.
Use the returned value with ar_parse_entry_at on the same archive/stream context.

functions.name: ar_entry_get_size
functions.description: Returns the total uncompressed size of the current entry. Read exactly this many bytes via ar_entry_uncompress across one or more calls.
requirements: ar must refer to a current, successfully parsed entry.
Use this size to govern the total number of bytes requested via ar_entry_uncompress; do not exceed this total.

functions.name: ar_entry_get_filetime
functions.description: Returns the stored modification timestamp of the current entry as 100-nanosecond intervals since 1601-01-01 (FILETIME epoch).
requirements: ar must refer to a current, successfully parsed entry.
Interpretation and conversion to other time bases is the caller's responsibility.

functions.name: ar_entry_uncompress
functions.description: Decompresses the next count bytes of the current entry into buffer. Returns false on error. Do not manually seek in the stream between ar_parse_entry and the last corresponding ar_entry_uncompress call.
requirements: ar must refer to a current, successfully parsed entry ready for extraction.
buffer must point to a writable memory region of at least count bytes.
The sum of counts over successive calls should not exceed ar_entry_get_size(ar).
Do not perform manual seeks/skips on the underlying stream until all requested uncompression for the entry is complete.

functions.name: ar_get_global_comment
functions.description: Copies up to count bytes of the archive’s global comment (if present) into buffer. Returns the actual number of bytes copied, or if buffer is NULL, the required buffer size.
requirements: ar must be a valid, initialized archive.
If buffer is non-NULL, it must point to a writable region of at least count bytes.
Passing buffer == NULL queries the size required to hold the full comment.

functions.name: ar_open_rar_archive
functions.description: Checks whether the stream contains RAR data and prepares the archive for listing/extraction. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable ar_stream positioned at the start of the RAR data.
The stream remains owned by the caller; close it with ar_close after ar_close_archive.

functions.name: ar_open_tar_archive
functions.description: Checks whether the stream contains TAR data and prepares the archive for listing/extraction. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable ar_stream positioned at the start of the TAR data.
The stream remains owned by the caller; close it with ar_close after ar_close_archive.

functions.name: ar_open_zip_archive
functions.description: Checks whether the stream contains ZIP data and prepares the archive for listing/extraction. Returns NULL on failure. Set deflatedonly when extracting formats (e.g., XPS, EPUB) that only allow Deflate compression.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable ar_stream positioned at the start of the ZIP data.
Choose deflatedonly = true when only Deflate-compressed entries should be supported per format constraints; otherwise false is acceptable.
The stream remains owned by the caller; close it with ar_close after ar_close_archive.

functions.name: ar_open_7z_archive
functions.description: Checks whether the stream contains 7Z data and prepares the archive for listing/extraction. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: stream must be a valid, readable ar_stream positioned at the start of the 7Z data.
The stream remains owned by the caller; close it with ar_close after ar_close_archive.

data_types.description: A valid path string to a readable file on the local filesystem. May include directories, extensions, and platform-appropriate separators. The content of the file referenced by the path is what downstream consumers read; the path itself must be a syntactically valid, existing file path.
An uninterpreted byte buffer of any length (including embedded NULs). Used when APIs accept raw memory and may treat it as archive bytes or other opaque data without assuming text encoding.

A textual string encoded in UTF-8, suitable for functions that expect human-readable names or identifiers. May include any valid Unicode code points encoded as UTF-8 and is NUL-terminated when passed as a C string.

import os
import io
import random
import struct
import tempfile
import zipfile
import tarfile
import time
from typing import Tuple

# This generator produces a valid filesystem path string (as bytes) to a
# readable temporary file containing a small, valid archive or raw data.
# It targets stubs ar_open and ar_open_file which both expect a filesystem path
# pointing to readable data. We create the file in the system temp directory,
# write valid contents (ZIP/TAR/7z-like header placeholder or generic bytes),
# and return the path bytes. The fuzzer harness will read from that path.
#
# Design goals:
# - Always return an existing, readable file path.
# - Generate a variety of valid archive formats and plain data.
# - Stay within 4096 bytes total file content.
# - Seeded randomness for reproducibility.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_ascii_filename(rng: random.Random, ext: str) -> str:
    # Generate a simple ASCII-safe filename to avoid path issues
    name = ''.join(rng.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_-') for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 16)))
    return f"fuzz_{name}{ext}"


def _write_bytes(path: str, data: bytes):
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(data[:MAX_SIZE])


def _make_plain_file(tmpdir: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a small random-but-valid binary blob. This may exercise raw stream reads.
    size = rng.randint(32, 1024)
    # Bias towards textual headers to look like archives occasionally
    prefixes = [b'', b'Rar!\x1A\x07\x00', b'PK\x03\x04', b"7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C"]
    prefix = rng.choice(prefixes)
    body = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(max(0, size - len(prefix))))
    data = prefix + bytes(body)
    fname = _rand_ascii_filename(rng, '.bin')
    path = os.path.join(tmpdir, fname)
    _write_bytes(path, data)
    return path


def _make_zip_file(tmpdir: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a minimal but valid ZIP with 1-3 files, varying compression.
    fname = _rand_ascii_filename(rng, '.zip')
    path = os.path.join(tmpdir, fname)
    # Use Python's zipfile to ensure validity.
    compression = rng.choice([zipfile.ZIP_STORED, zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED])
    # Some Python builds may not have zlib; fallback to stored if deflated unavailable
    if compression == zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED and not zipfile.zlib:
        compression = zipfile.ZIP_STORED
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, 'w', compression=compression) as zf:
        nfiles = rng.randint(1, 3)
        for i in range(nfiles):
            arcname = f"file_{i}_{rng.randint(0, 9999)}.txt"
            # Mix small text and small binary payloads
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                content = ("Hello from fuzz ZIP " + str(rng.randint(0, 1_000_000))).encode('utf-8')
            else:
                size = rng.randint(1, 256)
                content = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
            zf.writestr(arcname, content)
        # Optionally set a global comment (ZIP supports this)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            comment = ("ZIP comment " + str(rng.randint(0, 1_000_000))).encode('utf-8')
            # Truncate to limit total size
            zf.comment = comment[:128]
    # Ensure file is not oversized
    if os.path.getsize(path) > MAX_SIZE:
        # If too big, rewrite with fewer/smaller entries
        with zipfile.ZipFile(path, 'w', compression=zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as zf:
            zf.writestr('small.txt', b'A')
    return path


def _make_tar_file(tmpdir: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a minimal POSIX tar with 1-2 files. tarfile writes valid headers.
    fname = _rand_ascii_filename(rng, '.tar')
    path = os.path.join(tmpdir, fname)
    mode = rng.choice(['w', 'w:gz', 'w:bz2', 'w:xz'])
    # Some compressions may be unavailable; fall back silently
    for m in [mode, 'w', 'w:gz', 'w:bz2', 'w:xz']:
        try:
            with tarfile.open(path, m) as tf:
                nfiles = rng.randint(1, 2)
                for i in range(nfiles):
                    data = (f"hello tar {rng.randint(0, 1_000_000)}\n").encode('utf-8')
                    info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=f"item_{i}_{rng.randint(0, 9999)}.txt")
                    info.size = len(data)
                    info.mtime = int(time.time())
                    tf.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
            break
        except tarfile.TarError:
            continue
    # If size too large, rewrite uncompressed minimal
    if os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getsize(path) > MAX_SIZE:
        with tarfile.open(path, 'w') as tf:
            data = b'A' * 10
            info = tarfile.TarInfo(name='small.txt')
            info.size = len(data)
            tf.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
    return path


def _make_7z_like_file(tmpdir: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Python stdlib cannot create true 7z. We write a minimal 7z signature + small payload
    # to look like a 7z stream. Some consumers check signature first.
    # 7z signature: 37 7A BC AF 27 1C, then version bytes and other header fields.
    fname = _rand_ascii_filename(rng, '.7z')
    path = os.path.join(tmpdir, fname)
    sig = b"7z\xBC\xAF'\x1C"  # 6 bytes signature
    version = bytes([0x00, 0x04])  # arbitrary minor/major
    start_header_crc = struct.pack('<I', rng.getrandbits(32))
    next_header_offset = struct.pack('<Q', rng.randint(0, 64))
    next_header_size = struct.pack('<Q', rng.randint(0, 64))
    next_header_crc = struct.pack('<I', rng.getrandbits(32))
    header = sig + version + start_header_crc + next_header_offset + next_header_size + next_header_crc
    payload = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 128)))
    data = (header + payload)[:MAX_SIZE]
    _write_bytes(path, data)
    return path


def _make_rar_like_file(tmpdir: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Write RAR signature with small payload to simulate a RAR stream start.
    # RAR 4.x signature: 52 61 72 21 1A 07 00 ("Rar!\x1A\x07\x00")
    fname = _rand_ascii_filename(rng, '.rar')
    path = os.path.join(tmpdir, fname)
    sig = b'Rar!\x1A\x07\x00'
    payload = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(16, 256)))
    data = (sig + payload)[:MAX_SIZE]
    _write_bytes(path, data)
    return path


def _choose_builder(rng: random.Random):
    # Weighted selection to favor truly valid formats (zip/tar) but still cover signature-led ones.
    builders = [
        (_make_zip_file, 3.0),
        (_make_tar_file, 2.5),
        (_make_plain_file, 1.5),
        (_make_7z_like_file, 1.0),
        (_make_rar_like_file, 1.0),
    ]
    total = sum(w for _, w in builders)
    pick = rng.random() * total
    acc = 0.0
    for b, w in builders:
        acc += w
        if pick <= acc:
            return b
    return builders[0][0]


def _safe_temp_dir() -> str:
    # Use system temp dir; ensure it exists
    return tempfile.gettempdir()


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    tmpdir = _safe_temp_dir()

    builder = _choose_builder(rng)

    # To reduce collisions, ensure unique path by including random token
    # but keep simple ASCII chars.
    try:
        path = builder(tmpdir, rng)
    except Exception:
        # Fallback to plain file if builder fails for any reason
        path = _make_plain_file(tmpdir, rng)

    # Ensure file exists and is readable; otherwise fallback
    if not (isinstance(path, str) and os.path.isfile(path) and os.access(path, os.R_OK)):
        path = _make_plain_file(tmpdir, rng)

    # Return path as UTF-8 bytes; fuzzer expects a C string path
    return os.fsencode(path)

import random
import struct

# Generator for arbitrary binary data to feed ar_open_memory. We try to create
# small but valid-looking archive buffers (ZIP/TAR/7z/RAR) and some signature-
# prefixed random content. Keep under 4096 bytes and deterministic by seed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _zip_eocd(comment: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    # End of central directory record for empty archive
    sig = b"PK\x05\x06"
    disks = 0
    disk_central = 0
    entries_this = 0
    entries_total = 0
    cd_size = 0
    cd_offset = 0
    comment_len = len(comment)
    hdr = struct.pack("<4sHHHHIIH", sig, disks, disk_central, entries_this, entries_total, cd_size, cd_offset, comment_len)
    return (hdr + comment)[:MAX_SIZE]


def _zip_local_header(name: bytes, data: bytes, method: int = 0, extra: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    # Build a ZIP local file header + name + extra + data (no data descriptor)
    # Layout (little endian):
    # signature(4) = 0x04034b50, version needed(2), flags(2), method(2), mtime(2), mdate(2),
    # crc32(4), comp_size(4), uncomp_size(4), name_len(2), extra_len(2)
    sig = b"PK\x03\x04"
    ver_needed = 20
    flags = 0
    if method != 0:
        method = 0
    mtime = 0
    mdate = 0
    import zlib

    crc32 = zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    comp = data  # store
    comp_size = len(comp)
    uncomp_size = len(data)
    name_len = len(name)
    extra_len = len(extra)

    out = bytearray()
    out += sig
    out += struct.pack("<HHHHH", ver_needed, flags, method, mtime, mdate)
    out += struct.pack("<III", crc32, comp_size, uncomp_size)
    out += struct.pack("<HH", name_len, extra_len)
    out += name
    out += extra
    out += comp
    return bytes(out)


def _zip_central_header(name: bytes, local_offset: int, data: bytes, method: int = 0, extra: bytes = b"", comment: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    # Central directory file header
    # signature(4)=0x02014b50, ver_made(2), ver_needed(2), flags(2), method(2), mtime(2), mdate(2),
    # crc32(4), comp_size(4), uncomp_size(4), name_len(2), extra_len(2), comment_len(2),
    # disk_start(2), int_attr(2), ext_attr(4), rel_offset(4)
    sig = b"PK\x01\x02"
    ver_made = 20
    ver_needed = 20
    flags = 0
    if method != 0:
        method = 0
    mtime = 0
    mdate = 0
    import zlib

    crc32 = zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    comp_size = len(data)
    uncomp_size = len(data)
    name_len = len(name)
    extra_len = len(extra)
    comment_len = len(comment)
    disk_start = 0
    int_attr = 0
    ext_attr = 0
    rel_offset = local_offset

    out = bytearray()
    out += sig
    out += struct.pack("<HHHHH", ver_made, ver_needed, flags, method, mtime)
    out += struct.pack("<H", mdate)
    out += struct.pack("<III", crc32, comp_size, uncomp_size)
    out += struct.pack("<HHH", name_len, extra_len, comment_len)
    out += struct.pack("<HH", disk_start, int_attr)
    out += struct.pack("<I", ext_attr)
    out += struct.pack("<I", rel_offset)
    out += name
    out += extra
    out += comment
    return bytes(out)


def make_zip_empty(comment: bytes) -> bytes:
    return _zip_eocd(comment)


def make_zip_single_file(name: bytes, content: bytes, global_comment: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    local = _zip_local_header(name, content, method=0, extra=b"")
    local_offset = 0  # placed at start
    central = _zip_central_header(name, local_offset, content, method=0, extra=b"", comment=b"")
    cd_start = len(local)
    cd = central
    eocd = struct.pack(
        "<4sHHHHIIH",
        b"PK\x05\x06",
        0,
        0,
        1,
        1,
        len(cd),
        cd_start,
        len(global_comment),
    ) + global_comment
    return (local + cd + eocd)[:MAX_SIZE]


def make_7z_minimal() -> bytes:
    # 7z signature header
    sig = b"7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C"
    major, minor = 0, 4
    next_header_offset = 0
    next_header_size = 0
    next_header_crc = 0
    import zlib

    start = struct.pack("<QIQ", next_header_offset, next_header_size, next_header_crc)
    start_crc = zlib.crc32(start) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    header = bytearray()
    header += sig
    header += struct.pack("<BB", major, minor)
    header += struct.pack("<I", start_crc)
    header += start
    return bytes(header)


def _tar_checksum(block: bytearray) -> None:
    # Compute tar checksum over 512-byte header
    block[148:156] = b"        "
    total = sum(block)
    chksum = (oct(total)[2:]).encode("ascii")
    chksum = chksum.rjust(6, b"0") + b"\x00\x20"
    block[148:156] = chksum


def make_tar_with_file(name: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    hdr = bytearray(512)
    hdr[0:len(name[:100])] = name[:100]
    hdr[100:108] = b"0000777\0"
    hdr[108:116] = b"0000000\0"
    hdr[116:124] = b"0000000\0"
    size_o = (oct(len(data))[2:]).encode("ascii").rjust(11, b"0") + b"\0"
    hdr[124:136] = size_o
    hdr[136:148] = b"00000000000\0"
    hdr[156:157] = b"0"
    hdr[257:263] = b"ustar\0"
    hdr[263:265] = b"00"
    hdr[265:297] = b"user\0" + b"\0" * (32 - 5)
    hdr[297:329] = b"group\0" + b"\0" * (32 - 6)
    _tar_checksum(hdr)

    out = bytearray()
    out += hdr
    out += data
    pad = (-len(out)) % 512
    out += b"\0" * pad
    out += b"\0" * 1024
    return bytes(out[:MAX_SIZE])


def make_rar4_minimal() -> bytes:
    # RAR 4.x signature and a minimal archive header block
    sig = b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x00"
    # Build block body (type 0x73 = main), flags=0, size=13, plus 9 reserved bytes
    body = bytearray()
    body += b"\x73"  # type
    body += struct.pack("<H", 0)  # flags
    body += struct.pack("<H", 13)  # size
    body += b"\x00" * 9
    import zlib

    crc16 = zlib.crc32(bytes(body)) & 0xFFFF
    return sig + struct.pack("<H", crc16) + bytes(body)


def make_rar5_minimal() -> bytes:
    # RAR5 signature, then a tiny main header
    sig = b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x01\x00"
    import zlib

    block_type = 1  # main
    flags_varint = b"\x00"
    size_varint = b"\x00"
    body = bytes([block_type]) + flags_varint + size_varint
    crc = zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return sig + struct.pack("<I", crc) + body


def make_prefixed_random(prefix: bytes, rnd: random.Random, total_max: int = 512) -> bytes:
    max_body = max(0, min(total_max, MAX_SIZE) - len(prefix))
    size = rnd.randint(0, max_body)
    body = rnd.randbytes(size)
    return (prefix + body)[:MAX_SIZE]


CHOICES = [
    # ZIP empty archive
    lambda rnd: make_zip_empty(comment=rnd.choice([b"", b"fuzz", rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(0, 50))])),
    # ZIP single stored file
    lambda rnd: make_zip_single_file(
        name=rnd.choice([b"a.txt", b"dir/file.bin", b"unicode_\xE2\x98\x83.txt"]),
        content=rnd.choice([b"", b"hello", rnd.randbytes(rnd.randint(1, 64))]),
        global_comment=rnd.choice([b"", b"zipcomment"]),
    ),
    # 7z minimal
    lambda rnd: make_7z_minimal(),
    # TAR with one file
    lambda rnd: make_tar_with_file(
        name=rnd.choice([b"file", b"dir/file", b"longname_" + rnd.randbytes(8).hex().encode("ascii")])[:100],
        data=rnd.choice([b"", b"A" * rnd.randint(1, 200)]),
    ),
    # RAR4 minimal
    lambda rnd: make_rar4_minimal(),
    # RAR5 minimal
    lambda rnd: make_rar5_minimal(),
    # Random buffers with ZIP signatures
    lambda rnd: make_prefixed_random(b"PK\x03\x04", rnd, 256),
    lambda rnd: make_prefixed_random(b"PK\x05\x06", rnd, 64),
]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    data = rnd.choice(CHOICES)(rnd)
    if not data:
        data = b"\0"
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]

# This generator produces UTF-8 strings for entry names used by ar_parse_entry_for.

    + EPUB_LIKE

def _rand_path_component(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    s = []
    n = r.randint(1, max_len)
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.75:
            s.append(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE))
        else:
            seg = r.choice(UNICODE_SEGMENTS)
            s.append(seg)
    comp = "".join(s)
    comp = comp.replace("\x00", "")
    comp = comp.replace("/", "-").replace("\\", "-")
    return comp or "x"


def _random_entry_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.55:
        return r.choice(COMMON_SET)

    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = r.randint(0, 6)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append("./")
    elif r.random() < 0.1:
        parts.append("../")
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_path_component(r, max_len=r.randint(3, 20)))
        parts.append("/")
    base = _rand_path_component(r, max_len=r.randint(1, 40))

    if r.random() < 0.15:
        name = ("".join(parts)) + base + "/"
        return name

    ext = r.choice(COMMON_EXTS)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        base = base.upper()
    elif r.random() < 0.2:
        base = base.lower()

    if r.random() < 0.1:
        base = "." + base
    if r.random() < 0.05:
        base = base + "."

    name = ("".join(parts)) + base + ext

    if r.random() < 0.1:
        name = name.replace("/", r.choice(["/", "\\"]))

    enc = name.encode('utf-8')
    if len(enc) > 4000:
        enc = enc[-4000:]
        name = enc.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    return name


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    name = _random_entry_name(r)

    # Ensure valid UTF-8 and no embedded NULs
    name = name.replace("\x00", "")

    data = name.encode('utf-8')
    if not data:
        data = b"file"

    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
        try:
            data.decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            for i in range(4095, 0, -1):
                try:
                    data[:i].decode('utf-8')
                    data = data[:i]
                    break
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    continue
    return data
